title: Determining glioma cell invasion and proliferation in ex vivo organotypic mouse brain slices using whole-mount immunostaining and tissue clearing
protocol: Sacrifice a 16 days-old C57BL/6 mouse by exposure to CO2.
Decapitate the mouse using scissors.
Peel away the skin and meninges of the head until the skull becomes visible.
Place ultra-fine scissors in the spinal cord and cut until the cerebellum is reached.
Carefully peel away the skull meninges using forceps until the brain is uncovered.
With ultra-fine scissors, make a cut rostral of the olfactory bulb to disconnect the olfactory nerves.
Place forceps caudally under the brain and transfer the brain from the skull into a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL aCSF.
Place the tube with the brain on ice.
Take the vibratome equipment out of the buffer tray with 70% ethanol.
Remove the ethanol and let everything air-dry.
Pour the aCSF containing the brain(s) into a sterile Petri dish.
Remove the olfactory bulb and cerebellum using a sterile razor blade.
Place the brain on the razor blade with the rostral part facing upward.
Lightly touch the brain-blade interface with a paper tissue to remove residual aCSF from the caudal part.
Place a drop of Loctite 401 instant adhesive glue on the specimen disk.
Transfer the brain to the glue with the rostral part facing up.
Fixate the specimen disc with the mounted brain tissue in the buffer tray.
Fill the buffer tray with cold aCSF until the tissue is fully submerged (100 mL).
Place a filter tip connected to CO2 into the bucket to carbonate the aCSF.
Turn on the vibratome.
Set the frequency to 7 Hz and the slicing thickness to 350 μm.
Trim off the rostral region of the brain until the lateral ventricles become visible.
Take the culture plate with cell inserts out of the incubator.
Place a sterile spoon underneath the blade.
Transfer tissue with visible lateral ventricles to the spoon using a sterile brush.
Pour off most of the aCSF and transfer the brain slice to a cell culture insert.
Collect four slices per insert.
Remove residual aCSF from each insert using a P1000 pipette with filter tip.
Take the plate to a cell culture laminar flow cabinet.
Wash the slices once with sterile PBS.
Transfer the cell culture inserts to the culture plate with serum-supplemented recovery medium after PBS wash (optional).
Place the plate with cell culture inserts containing brain slices in serum-supplemented recovery medium into a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2 for overnight recovery (minimum 24 hours).
Passage the cells used for the experiment with standard passaging methods.
Make cell suspensions of 2.5 × 10^4 cells/μL.
Prepare a 6-well plate with 1 mL neural stem cell (NSC)-medium per insert.
Prepare a 6-well plate with 2 wells with 1 mL PBS per insert.
Take the cell culture inserts with ex vivo organotypic brain slices from the incubator.
Dip the inserts two times in 1 mL PBS.
Remove the remaining recovery medium from the inserts and transfer the inserts to the 6-well plate with NSC-medium.
Clean your working space with 70% ethanol.
Fixate the micromanipulator at the dissection microscope using the magnetic stand.
Place the Hamilton syringe in the micromanipulator.
Clean the syringe by washing it first with acetone.
Wash the syringe multiple times with 70% ethanol.
Rinse the syringe with PBS.
Orient the plate with organotypic brain slices and the micromanipulator under the dissection microscope.
Place the 6-well plate containing the organotypic brain slices under the dissection microscope and remove the lid.
Move the micromanipulator to ensure that the syringe is centered at 4× magnification when touching the brain slices.
Mix the cell suspension with a normal pipette.
Take up 0.5 μL of the mixed cell suspension with the syringe using a normal pipette.
Using the micromanipulator, move the syringe towards the brain slice.
Slowly insert the syringe approximately 50 μm into the lateral ventricle at an angle of about 45 degrees.
Retract the syringe out of the tissue by 40 μm after insertion.
Inject the cell suspension slowly (∼30 seconds per 0.5 μL) to prevent flushing over the tissue.
Slowly withdraw the syringe after injection is complete.
Rinse the syringe with PBS multiple times before injecting the next cell line.
After all injections, rinse the syringe thoroughly with PBS, followed by 70% ethanol and acetone.
Inspect the organotypic brain slices with a fluorescent microscope to check for the presence of fluorescently labeled cells.
Place the culture plate in the incubator to culture the ex vivo organotypic brain slices.
Replace the medium of the injected organotypic brain slices once every 2 or 3 days with fresh prewarmed NSC-medium.
At day 8, after 7 days post cell injection, fixate the ex vivo organotypic brain slices.
Wash the cell culture inserts containing the brain slices one time with PBS.
Place the inserts in 2 mL 4% PFA in PBS (covered from light) at 4°C overnight (minimum 12 hours).
The next day, wash the inserts three times with PBS.
Store the washed inserts at 4°C until further use.
Cut the membrane from the inserts around the individual brain slices using a scalpel.
Transfer the membrane with the brain slice attached to it to a 24-well plate.
Permeabilize the brain slices in 500 μL 2% PBST (2% Triton-X100 in PBS) at room temperature for 4 h.
Add 500 μL PBS-GT to the brain slices.
Incubate the brain slices at room temperature overnight (minimum 12 hours).
Prepare primary antibody mix by adding rabbit anti-laminin and chicken anti-vimentin antibodies to PBS-GT with 0.1% saponin, making 250 μL per sample.
Add the primary antibody mix to the brain slices and incubate at 37°C on a horizontal shaker (70 rpm) for 72 hours.
Wash the brain slices six times with PBS-T (0.5% Triton-X100 in PBS) for one hour each wash step at room temperature.
Prepare secondary antibody mix by adding donkey anti-rabbit-Cy3 and donkey anti-chicken-AF647 antibodies to PBS-GT with 0.1% saponin, making 250 μL per sample.
Add the secondary antibody mix to the brain slices and incubate at 37°C on a horizontal shaker (70 rpm) for 24 hours protected from light.
Wash the brain slices six times with PBS-T at room temperature for one hour each wash step.
Pre-warm RapiClear 1.47 solution at 37°C.
Add 300 μL of pre-warmed RapiClear solution to each brain slice.
Place the brain slice container on a horizontal shaker at 37°C.
Incubate for a minimum of 45 minutes until the brain slice is transparent.
Transfer the brain slices to a glass microscopy slide.
Place an iSpacer on the glass microscopy slide.
Mount the brain slices within the iSpacer on the slide.
Fill the iSpacer with fresh RapiClear solution and seal with a coverslip.
Use clear nail polish to seal the edges of the coverslip.
Store the microscopy slides at 4°C until further use.
Transfer the brain to the iSpacer using a spatula if necessary.
Orient the membrane in such a way that it is on the bottom of the glass microscopy slide for imaging purposes.
Place the microscopy slide with the cleared brain slices on the stage of a confocal microscope with the coverslip facing the 10× objective.
Navigate to the region of interest using the microscope.
Adjust the laser power and gain to optimize the signal based on background and fluorescent signal.
Adjust the number and size of tiles for imaging.
Set the top and bottom of the z-stack appropriately to capture all cells.
Open the confocal-generated and tiled image in ImageJ.
Create a selection of the laminin signal around the tumor core (laminin deposits).
Go to a z-plane where the nuclei are clearly visible.
Open the Brightness & Contrast (Image > Adjust > Brightness & Contrast).
Linearly increase the laminin signal by sliding the bar above ‘Maximum’ to the left.
Stop adjusting the histogram until the laminin signal in and around the nuclei becomes clearly visible (= laminin deposit).
Duplicate the channel with the laminin staining (Image > Duplicate).
Duplicate the hyperstack for the laminin channel only, for all slices.
Open the ROI manager (Analyze > Tools > ROI manager).
Go to the first plane in the z-stack.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) around the laminin signal of the tumor core.
Select polygon selection tool.
Determine the border of the tumor core based on the laminin deposit and the density of the nuclei.
In the ROI manager, go to ‘More>Specify’ if no tumor core is visible.
Type the value 1 in ‘Width’, ‘Height’, ‘X coordinate’, and ‘Y coordinate’ and leave the ‘Slice’ value at the plane of interest.
Click OK to add a selection of 1 by 1 pixel to the ROI manager.
Repeat step for all other z-planes.
Save the ROIs in a designated folder (ROI manager > More> Save).
Open the ‘Macro’ tool of ImageJ (Plugins > Macros > Startup macros).
Create a new file in the ‘Macros’ tool (File > New).
Select the Macro language (Language > IJ1 Macro).
Copy and paste the script into the ‘Macros’ tool.
Run the macro to delete laminin signal outside of the tumor core in every plane.
Merge the laminin deposits channel with the original file.
Split the original file into separate channels (Image > Color > Split Channels).
Merge the separate channels of the original file with the laminin tumor core channel.
Select ‘Shortest Distance to Surfaces Surfaces = x’ in the dropdown menu, where x corresponds to the name of the surface of the laminin tumor core.
Click on the ‘Save’ icon to export the list as an excel file.
Click on the ‘Color’ icon to visualize the distribution of nuclei.
For ‘Color Type’, select ‘Statistics Coded’.
Select ‘Shortest Distance to Surfaces Surfaces = x’ in the dropdown menu for color coding, where x corresponds to the surface name.
Perform distance transformation on the created surface using the 'Tools' option followed by selecting 'Distance Transformation'.
Choose 'Outside SurfaceObject' when prompted for options during the MATLAB script execution within Imaris.
Repeat the ‘Distance Transformation’, this time select ‘Inside SurfaceObject’.
Calculate the distance from individual spots (nuclei) to the created surface (laminin tumor core).
Select the created spots and click on ‘Statistics’ then go to ‘Detailed’.
In the second dropdown menu, select ‘Intensity Center Ch = x Img 1’ for the channel created during step 56b (Outside SurfaceObject).
Click on the ‘Save’ Icon to export the data as an excel file.
Repeat the ‘Intensity Center Ch= x Img 1’ step for the channel created during step 56c (Inside SurfaceObject).
Click on the ‘Save’ Icon to export the data as an excel file.
Visualize the distribution of nuclei.
Click on the ‘Color’ icon and select ‘Statistics Coded’ in the dropdown menu.
Select ‘Intensity Center Ch= x Img 1’ for either channel created during steps 56b or 56c.
Prepare organotypic brain slices as described in previous steps.
Inject glioma cells into the prepared brain slices.
On the 7th day after injection, place a drop of 50 μL 40 mM BrdU in NSC-medium on top of the lateral ventricles containing the glioma cells.
Incubate at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 6 hours.
Cut the membrane around individual brain slices and transfer to an embedding mold.
Submerge brain slices in 30% sucrose in PBS (pH = 7.2) and incubate at 4°C for 48 h.
Remove the sucrose solution and wash the slices once with PBS.
Add Tissue Tek to the brain slices.
Place the embedding molds in 2-Methylbutan (-55°C) on dry-ice for 2 min until Tissue Tek is frozen.
Transfer snap-frozen brain slices to a cryostat with chamber temperature of -20°C and objective temperature of -18°C.
Use the cryostat to section the brain slices into 20 μm sections.
Attach the tissue to a SuperFrost Plus Adhesion microscope slide.
Collect tissue on different microscopy slides in series of four or five.
Orient the brain slice at the right angle relative to the knife of the cryostat.
Let the sections dry at room temperature until the Tissue Tek has evaporated.
Air dry the glass microscope slides taken from −20°C in an incubation box.
Wash the tissue three times with PBS to remove remaining traces of Tissue Tek.
Cover the tissue sections with HCl 2 N and incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Incubate the tissue sections in Borate Buffer at room temperature for 15 min.
Wash the tissue sections three times in PBS with 0.25% Triton-X100.
Dab the edges of the glass microscope slides carefully with a tissue paper without touching the brain tissue.
Delimit the area around the brain tissue with a hydrophobic pen to minimize antibody volume.
Incubate the tissue sections in blocking buffer at room temperature for 90 min.
Add BrdU primary antibodies to blocking buffer diluted 1:1 in PBS.
Prepare 100–300 μL of antibody mix per microscopy slide, dependent on the size of the delimited area.
Place the microscopy slides with tissue sections in a humidified chamber by placing wet paper tissues in the incubation box.
Incubate the tissue sections at 4°C overnight (minimum 12 hours).
Wash the tissue sections three times for 5–10 min with PBS on a shaker.
Add secondary antibodies and Hoechst to PBS with 0.25% triton.
Prepare 100–300 μL of secondary antibody mix per microscopy slide, dependent on the size of the delimited area.
Place the microscopy slides in a humidified chamber.
Add the secondary antibody mix and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour, protected from light.
Wash the tissue sections three times with PBS, protected from light.
Mount the glass microscope slides with a coverslip.
Hold the glass microscope slide vertically on a paper tissue to remove PBS.
Place three drops of FluorSave reagent or an alternative mounting solution on one side of the microscopy slide.
Slowly lower a 25 × 60 mm coverslip onto the mounting solution drops, spreading the mounting solution over the slide.
Remove excess mounting solution by placing the microscope slide on a paper tissue.
Let the microscope slide dry overnight at room temperature before imaging with epifluorescence microscopy or alternative imaging methods.
